title: REST vs GraphQL
sources: GraphQL Foundation, 'Introduction to GraphQL' graphql.org/learn (clients ask for exactly the fields they need and get a predictable response; typically served from a single endpoint)
AWS AppSync docs, 'Why use GraphQL' (over-fetching and under-fetching with fixed-shape REST responses; one request can return related data)
Fielding, 'Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures', ch.5 (REST; cacheable resources identified by URL)
MDN Web Docs, 'HTTP caching' (responses to GET requests are cacheable by URL; POST responses generally are not)
The two-request example, field names and the verdict are simplified and illustrative; a well-designed REST API can embed related data

lines.text: Your app needs a user's name and their latest posts, so how many requests is that?
With REST, it's often two: one endpoint for the user, another for the posts.
And each endpoint sends back a fixed shape, so you also get fields you never asked for.
lines.caps: A FIXED *SHAPE | FIELDS YOU *NEVER ASKED FOR

lines.text: That's over fetching, and needing a second trip is under fetching.
GraphQL flips it: there's one endpoint, and you write the exact shape you want.
lines.caps: *GRAPHQL FLIPS IT | ONE *ENDPOINT | YOU WRITE THE *SHAPE

lines.text: So you send a query asking for the name and three post titles,
and one response comes back with exactly those fields, nothing extra.
But here's the catch: everything goes through one endpoint, so simple URL based caching gets harder.
lines.caps: BUT HERE'S THE *CATCH | ONE *ENDPOINT | *CACHING GETS HARDER

lines.text: And a deeply nested query can make the server do far more work than it looks.
So REST is simple and cache friendly, and GraphQL is flexible but needs more care.
Pick by who's asking: fixed needs, REST; many different needs, GraphQL.
